title: Towards the Implementation of Magnetic Hysteresis into Electron Optical Calculations
content: Magnetic materials used for designing electron optical lenses are essential for the overall performance of these components and, ultimately, for the performance of entire electron microscopes [1]. Their optimal properties, annealing processes, etc., have been extensively studied over the past decades. Combined with modern simulation tools for electron optics design, a solid foundation for new electron optical microscopes is now available. However, magnetic hysteresis represents an unwanted aspect of these materials. Although it is purposefully reduced, it cannot be fully eliminated and negatively impacts electron beam stability, reproducibility, and dependence on excitation history. Here, we present the implementation of a Hysteresis module into the Electron Optics Design (EOD) software [2].
